assertion_results.text: States that jwt.decode does not verify the signature (token is forgeable) — distinct from just 'trusting the role claim'
assertion_results.evidence: "`jwt.decode()` only base64-decodes the token and never checks the signature. An attacker can write any token with a payload of `{"role":"admin"}`"

assertion_results.text: Describes the exploit: forge/modify a token to role=admin (or alg=none) to bypass auth
assertion_results.evidence: "An attacker can write any token with a payload of `{"role":"admin"}`, using any signature or `alg:none`, and send it in `Authorization`. The check on line 2 passes."

assertion_results.text: Fix: verify the signature with jwt.verify (key + expiry) before trusting any claim
assertion_results.evidence: "use `jwt.verify(token, key, { algorithms: ['RS256'] ... })`... Only read claims after `verify` succeeds. `verify` also enforces `exp` and `nbf`"

assertion_results.text: Rates it Critical/High and follows the exploit + impact + fix format
assertion_results.evidence: "### 🔴 Critical 1. Authentication: JWT decoded without verifying its signature" followed by "- Exploit: ... - Impact: ... - Fix: ..."
